item.title: - “Venerable sir, do you know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings?” - “Friend, I know the release, the escape, the seclusion for…
item.description:
- “Venerable sir, do you know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings?”
- “Friend, I know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings.”
- “But how, venerable sir, do you know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings?”
The destruction of delight in renewed existence,
The cessation of perception and consciousness,
The stilling of feelings —
Thus, friend, I know the release,
The escape and seclusion
For all kinds of beings.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.2

item.title: “Monks, having heard Brahmā’s request, out of compassion for beings, I surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye. With the Buddha-eye, I saw beings with little…
item.description:
“Monks, having heard Brahmā’s request, out of compassion for beings, I surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye. With the Buddha-eye, I saw beings with little dust in their eyes and with much dust in their eyes, with sharp faculties and with dull faculties, with good dispositions and with bad dispositions, some easy to teach and some hard to teach, and a few who saw the danger in rebirth to another world and the danger of faulty actions. Just as in a blue lotus pond, a red lotus pond, or a white lotus pond, some blue lotuses, red lotuses, or white lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, and do not rise above the water, being nourished underwater; some are born in the water, grow in the water, and reach the water’s surface; some are born in the water, grow in the water, and rise up above the water, not wetted by the water.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 26 – Ariyapariyesanāsutta

item.title: All conditioned things are truly impermanent, They arise and then pass away — Their nature is always thus. They come into being, Then they again…
item.description:
All conditioned things are truly impermanent,
They arise and then pass away —
Their nature is always thus.
They come into being,
Then they again are destroyed.
Blissful indeed when they
Are calmed and at peace.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 17 – Mahāsudassanasutta

item.title: “And how, monks, is there non-restraint? Here, monks, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is attached to agreeable forms and repelled…
item.description:
“And how, monks, is there non-restraint? Here, monks, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is attached to agreeable forms and repelled by disagreeable forms. He dwells with bodily mindfulness unestablished, with a limited mind. He does not know as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Here, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are not abandoned without remainder. Thus, monks, is non-restraint.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.244

item.title: Then the female demon Arati (Discontent) recited this verse to the Blessed One: How does a monk, Living amidst many obstacles, Having crossed the five…
item.description:
Then the female demon Arati (Discontent) recited this verse to the Blessed One:
How does a monk,
Living amidst many obstacles,
Having crossed the five floods,
Strive to cross the sixth?
How can he meditate,
Amidst many sensual perceptions,
So that they remain outside him,
Not catching him?

(The Blessed One):
With body tranquilized,
With mind well liberated,
With no more activities,
Mindful, without clinging,
Knowing the Dhamma,
Without thought, meditating —
Without anger, without distraction,
Without drowsiness, without laziness —
Thus the monk,
Living amidst many obstacles,
Having crossed the five floods,
Strives to cross the sixth.
Thus he meditates,
Amidst many sensual perceptions,
They remain outside him,
Not catching him.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 4.25

item.title: “Brahmin, if an elder is eighty, ninety, or a hundred years old, and he enjoys sensual pleasures, dwells amidst sensual pleasures, is burned by the…
item.description:
“Brahmin, if an elder is eighty, ninety, or a hundred years old, and he enjoys sensual pleasures, dwells amidst sensual pleasures, is burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, consumed by sensual thoughts, and strives for sensual pleasures — such a person is called a fool, not an elder. But if a young person, brahmin, a youth with black hair, endowed with the blessing of youth, in the prime of life, does not enjoy sensual pleasures, does not dwell amidst sensual pleasures, is not burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, not consumed by sensual thoughts, and does not strive for sensual pleasures — such a person is called a wise one, an elder.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 2.38

item.title: “Truly, monks, it is impossible that one could enjoy sensual pleasures apart from sensual pleasures, apart from sensual perceptions, apart from sensual thoughts.”
item.description:
“Truly, monks, it is impossible that one could enjoy sensual pleasures apart from sensual pleasures, apart from sensual perceptions, apart from sensual thoughts.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 22 – Alagaddūpamasutta

item.title: “Ānanda, here a monk abides contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having restrained covetousness and sorrow in the world; abides contemplating…
item.description:
“Ānanda, here a monk abides contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having restrained covetousness and sorrow in the world; abides contemplating feelings as feelings … mind as mind … phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having restrained covetousness and sorrow in the world. Ānanda, thus a monk is an island unto himself, a refuge unto himself, seeking no other refuge; with the Dhamma as his island, with the Dhamma as his refuge, seeking no other refuge.”

From: Dīgha Nikāya 16 – Mahāparinibbānasutta

item.title: “Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When…
item.description:
“Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is no basis, consciousness does not become established. When consciousness is not established and does not grow, there is no descent of name-and-form. With the cessation of name-and-form, the six sense-bases cease … such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.39

item.title: “The stream of craving flows everywhere, The creeper of craving sprouts and stands. Seeing that creeper that has arisen, Cut its root with wisdom.” “People,…
item.description:
“The stream of craving flows everywhere,
The creeper of craving sprouts and stands.
Seeing that creeper that has arisen,
Cut its root with wisdom.”

“People, immersed in sensual pleasures,
Delight in various pleasures.
Though they seek happiness,
They undergo birth and aging.”

“People bound by craving,
Thrashing about, terrified,
Like hares caught in a snare —
Bound by craving,
They undergo suffering for a long time.”

“People bound by craving,
Thrashing about, terrified,
Like hares caught in a snare —
Therefore, a monk who desires his own dispassion
Should abandon craving.”

From: Dhammapada 334-359
